entities.summary: Ithobaal II was the eighth-century BC Phoenician king of Tyre who paid tribute to the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III in 738 BCE, leaving behind a legacy of regional instability in the ancient Near East. His reign, marked by a single notable event, had a lasting impact on the politics of the region, as his successor Hiram II continued the tribute to the Assyrians. The significance of Ithobaal II lies in his role as a regional player, whose actions and decisions had far-reaching consequences for the ancient world. Ithobaal II's reign was a pivotal moment in the history of the Phoenician city-state of Tyre, which would continue to play a significant role in the region's politics and trade for centuries to come. Despite the brevity of his reign, Ithobaal II left an enduring mark on the ancient Near East, a testament to the enduring power of regional players in shaping the course of history.
